Mother of Alexander the Great and de facto ruler of Macedon during his conquests, which ancient Greek princess was eventually defeated and executed by Cassander?
Olympias: Mother of Alexander the Great (c. 375–316 BC)
A teacher, barrister and poet, this leader of the 1916 Easter Rising became, after his execution alongside fifteen others, the very embodiment of the rebellion in Irish eyes — who was he?
Known from early medieval carved stones, this people lived north of the Firth of Forth before merging with Dál Riata to form the Kingdom of Alba — who were they?
Picts: Medieval tribal confederation in northern Britain.
He ascended a throne at age two in 1908, then later reigned as a puppet emperor for a wartime Japanese state and was held as a war criminal until 1959 — which last emperor of China is he?
Puyi: Emperor of China (1908–1912) and of Manchukuo (1934–1945)
This centuries-long string of campaigns by northern Iberian Christian kingdoms drew to a close in 1492 with the fall of Granada, ending all Muslim rule on the peninsula — by what name is it known?
The eldest son of a U.S. president assassinated in 1865, this lawyer was the only one of his parents' four children to live past 18, and later served as Secretary of War — who is he?
Robert Todd Lincoln: American lawyer and politician (1843–1926)
A 1st-century man of Nazareth married to Mary and regarded as the legal father of Jesus, he was later declared protector of the Catholic Church by Pope Pius IX — who was he?

Saint Joseph: Husband of Mary and legal father of Jesus. According to the canonical Gospels, Joseph was a 1st-century Jewish man of Nazareth who was married to Mary, the mother of Jesus, and was the legal father of Jesus.

Angered by how territory was divided after an earlier 1912-13 conflict, Bulgaria attacked its former allies Serbia and Greece in mid-1913, only to be beaten back on multiple fronts as Romania invaded from the north and the Ottomans reclaimed lost ground — which conflict?
Second Balkan War: Bulgaria's invasion of its neighbours (1913)
Dubbed the 'Father of Japanese capitalism,' this Meiji-era business magnate founded the country's first joint-stock bank and the Tokyo Stock Exchange — who is he?
The 33rd king and founder of the Tibetan Empire, he formally brought Buddhism to Tibet, built the Jokhang, and moved his capital to Lhasa while his minister devised the Tibetan script. Who was he?
Songtsen Gampo: 1st Tibetan Emperor and 33rd King of Tibet (d.650)

At 25 she became Haryana's youngest-ever cabinet minister, and in 1998 she made history as Delhi's first female chief minister — who was this Indian diplomat who later ran external affairs under Modi?
This Thai telecom tycoon founded the mobile operator AIS, became one of the country's richest people, then won a landslide to become prime minister in 2001 — until a 2006 coup. Who is he?
Thaksin Shinawatra: Prime Minister of Thailand from 2001 to 2006.
Born Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, this British far-right activist co-founded and led the English Defence League from 2009 to 2013 — by what better-known name does he go?

Tommy Robinson: British far-right activist (born 1982). Stephen Christopher Yaxley-Lennon (né Yaxley; born 27 November 1982), better known as Tommy Robinson, is a British far-right, counter-jihad activist.
This Russian dissident and writer founded and chaired the Democratic Union party and sat on the editorial board of The New Times before her death in 2014 — who is she?
At 52, he became the youngest person to hold Vietnam's presidency since reunification, then resigned after just over a year amid an anti-corruption campaign — who is he?
Võ Văn Thưởng: President of Vietnam from 2023 to 2024.
As Lincoln's Secretary of State this anti-slavery Republican steered Union diplomacy through the Civil War and negotiated the treaty to buy the Alaska Territory — who is he?
After defeating his half-brother Sviatopolk in a war for the throne, this son of Vladimir the Great ruled Kiev from 1019 to 1054 — who was he?
Yaroslav the Wise: Grand Prince of Kiev from 1019 to 1054.

The first woman and youngest person ever to hold Slovakia's presidency, this lawyer and environmental activist won the 2016 Goldman Environmental Prize for fighting a toxic landfill in her hometown. Who is she?
Zuzana Čaputová: President of Slovakia from 2019 to 2024.
Which of these four was born earliest?
Jīvaka (born 401 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is the eldest?
Stephen Hales (born 1677) is the earliest of the four.
Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is the oldest?
Python (programming language) (founded 1991) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these is an astronomer?
Aristarchus of Samos is an astronomer. According to Ptolemy, Aristarchus observed the summer solstice of 280 BC.
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
Claude Shannon is a mathematician. Shannon was the first to describe the use of Boolean algebra—essential to all digital electronic circuits—and helped found the field of artificial intelligence.
What is the atomic number of Tantalum?
Tantalum is a chemical element; it has symbol Ta and atomic number 73.
What is the atomic number of Copper?
Copper is a chemical element; it has symbol Cu (from Latin cuprum) and atomic number 29.
In what year was Steve Jobs born?
Steve Jobs: Steven Paul Jobs (February 24, 1955 – October 5, 2011) was an American businessman, inventor, and investor.
In what year was Charles Babbage born?
Charles Babbage (26 December 1791 – 18 October 1871) was an English polymath.
In what year was Al-Khwarizmi born?
Al-Khwarizmi: Few biographical details are known about al-Khwarizmi's life.
In what year did Ratan Tata die?
Ratan Tata: Ratan Naval Tata (28 December 1937 – 9 October 2024) was an Indian industrialist and philanthropist.
In what year did Johannes Gutenberg die?
Johannes Gutenberg: Johannes Gensfleisch zur Laden zum Gutenberg (c. 1393–1406 – 3 February 1468) was a German inventor and craftsman who invented the movable-type printing press.
In what year was Ceres discovered?
Ceres is a dwarf planet in the main asteroid belt between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
Azithromycin: Pfizer. It is administered by mouth, into a vein, or as topical treatment for the eye.
In which country is Royal Society?
Royal Society: United Kingdom. Founded on 28 November 1660, it was granted a royal charter by King Charles II and is the oldest continuously existing scientific academy in the world.
Who is credited with discovering Archaeopteryx?
Archaeopteryx: Carl Friedrich Häberlein. Archaeopteryx (lit. 'ancient wing'), sometimes referred to by its German name, "Urvogel " (lit. 'Primeval Bird') is an extinct genus of bird-like dinosaurs.
Who is credited with discovering Oganesson?
Oganesson: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Oganesson is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Og and atomic number 118.
Who is credited with discovering Cimetidine?
Cimetidine: John Colin Emmett. Cimetidine, sold under the brand name Tagamet among others, is a histamine H2 receptor antagonist that inhibits stomach acid production.
Who is credited with discovering Iridium?
Iridium: Smithson Tennant. Iridium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ir and atomic number 77.
Bred for strength and endurance to haul heavy loads across the snow, this large sled-dog breed shares its arctic heritage with breeds like the Siberian Husky and Samoyed — what breed is it?
Alaskan Malamute is a large breed of dog that was originally bred for its strength and endurance to haul heavy freight as a sled dog.

Having led the explosive growth of the American steel industry, this Scottish-American industrialist gave away almost 90 percent of his fortune — about $350 million — in the final 18 years of his life — who is he?
Andrew Carnegie (November 25, 1835 - August 11, 1919) was a Scottish-American industrialist and philanthropist.
Excavated in Argentina starting in 1989 under paleontologist José Bonaparte, this Late Cretaceous titanosaur weighed as much as 80 tons — which genus of giant sauropod?
Argentinosaurus (meaning "lizard from Argentina") is a genus of giant sauropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period in what is now Argentina.

Originating in Central Africa and classified as a hound by the American Kennel Club, this dog breed doesn't bark but instead makes an unusual yodel-like sound due to its uniquely shaped larynx — what's the breed?
Basenji is a breed of hunting dog created from stock that originated in Central Africa, including in the Republic of the Congo and other adjacent tropical African countries.
Caused by a recessive allele in the leopard but a dominant one in the jaguar, this dark melanistic variant still secretly carries its usual rosettes — what is it called?
Black panther is the melanistic colour variant of the leopard (Panthera pardus) and the jaguar (Panthera onca).

This shield-shaped insect, native to East Asia, was accidentally introduced to Allentown, Pennsylvania in 1998 and became a major agricultural pest feeding on over 100 plant species — what insect is it?
Brown marmorated stink bug (Halyomorpha halys) is an insect in the family Pentatomidae, native to China, Japan, Korea, and other Asian regions.

Made of one oxygen atom triple-bonded to a single atom of the element that also forms diamonds and graphite, this colorless, odorless, poisonous gas is slightly less dense than air and typically arises from incomplete combustion — name the compound?
Carbon monoxide (chemical formula CO) is a poisonous, flammable gas that is colorless, odorless, tasteless, and slightly less dense than air.

Native to North America except for one species found mostly in Asia, these small striped rodents are technically classified as squirrels and pack food into cheek pouches for winter storage — what are they?
Chipmunk are small, striped squirrels of subtribe Tamiina.

Making up 25 to 35 percent of protein content in mammals, this triple-helix structural protein is the main component of the extracellular matrix in cartilage, bone, tendons, and skin — name the protein?
Collagen is the main structural protein in the extracellular matrix of the connective tissues of many animals.

The first anatomically modern humans known to inhabit Europe and Siberia, arriving as early as 56,800 years ago, this population interbred with the indigenous Neanderthals before the latter went extinct — who are they?
Cro-Magnon (EEMH) were the first early modern humans (Homo sapiens) found in Europe and Siberia, continuously occupying the continent possibly from as early as 56,800 years ago.
This biological process breaks down large insoluble food compounds into small water-soluble components for absorption into the bloodstream, via both mechanical and chemical means. What is it?
Digestion is the breakdown of large insoluble food compounds into small water-soluble components so that they can be absorbed into the blood plasma.

This American theoretical physicist, a professor emeritus at Princeton's Institute for Advanced Study, is renowned for foundational contributions to string theory and topological quantum field theory — who is he?
Edward Witten (born August 26, 1951) is an American theoretical physicist known for his contributions to string theory, topological quantum field theory, and various areas of mathematics.
This class of chemical compounds forms when the hydrogen of an acid's hydroxyl group is replaced by a carbon-based group, and includes the fatty-acid derivatives called glycerides. What is it?
Ester is a compound derived from an acid (either organic or inorganic) in which the hydrogen atom (H) of at least one acidic hydroxyl group (OH) of that acid is replaced by an organyl group (R).

Species in the stinging genus Solenopsis are sometimes confused with unrelated weaver insects in Southeast Asia that share their reddish color and painful bite — what's the common name for this group?
Fire ant are several species of ants in the genus Solenopsis, which includes over 200 species.
Caused by abnormalities in the genome, this category of health problem may arise from a single faulty gene, many genes, or a chromosome abnormality — what is the general term?
Genetic disorder is a health problem caused by one or more abnormalities in the genome.
What common name covers a diverse family of marine ray-finned fish in the order Perciformes, most belonging to the genera Epinephelus or Mycteroperca?
Grouper are a diverse group of marine ray-finned fish in the family Epinephelidae, in the order Perciformes.
Named after the physicist who first proved the existence of electromagnetic waves, this SI unit measures one cycle per second. What unit is it?
Hertz (symbol: Hz) is the unit of frequency in the International System of Units (SI), often described as being equivalent to one event (or cycle) per second.
Triggered by causes like vomiting, diarrhea, or the diuretic furosemide, this condition denotes a blood potassium level under 3.5 mmol/L — what is it?
Hypokalemia is a low level of potassium (K+) in the blood serum.
Known for the mantra 'Dying is not a crime,' this euthanasia advocate served eight years in prison after his fourth trial ended in a murder conviction — who is he?
Jack Kevorkian (May 26, 1928 - June 3, 2011), also known by the nickname "Dr.
While tinkering with electromagnets, which American physicist discovered self-inductance and later became the very first secretary of the Smithsonian Institution?
Joseph Henry (December 17, 1797- May 13, 1878) was an American physicist and inventor who served as the first secretary of the Smithsonian Institution.

Sold under a well-known brand name, this medication treats several types of epilepsy including focal and tonic-clonic seizures, and also helps stabilize mood by reducing future depressive episodes in bipolar disorder — which drug?
Lamotrigine (luh-), sold under the brand name Lamictal among others, is a medication used to treat epilepsy and stabilize mood in bipolar disorder.
Named after a pioneer of sterile surgery, this genus of rod-shaped bacteria can multiply even at refrigerator temperatures and causes a rare but serious foodborne illness — what is it?
Listeria is a genus of bacteria that acts as an intracellular parasite in mammals.
Formed from two glucose units linked by an alpha(1→4) bond, which disaccharide, a reducing sugar unlike sucrose, is released when starch breaks down during malting?
Maltose (or), also known as maltobiose or malt sugar, is a disaccharide formed from two units of glucose joined with an (14) bond.
A waxy crystalline compound from peppermint and corn mint, it triggers a cooling sensation and works as a mild local anesthetic to soothe a sore throat — what is it?
Menthol is a monoterpenoid organic compound that occurs naturally in the oils of certain plants in the mint family, such as corn mint and peppermint.
Also called a mutt, this designation covers any dog outside official breed standards — with an estimated 150 million examples worldwide, believed to enjoy 'hybrid vigor' — what's it called?
Mongrel is any dog which does not belong to one officially recognized breed.

Distinguished from flatworms by having a digestive tract with openings at both ends, these free-living or parasitic roundworms make up their own entire phylum found in nearly every environment on Earth — what are they?
Nematode (or NEEM-; Ancient), roundworms or eelworms constitute the phylum Nematoda.
Despite the zebra-like stripes on its legs, this shy mammal of the northeastern Congo is actually the giraffe's only living cousin — and the sole other member of the family Giraffidae. What is it?
Okapi (Okapia johnstoni), also known as the forest giraffe, and zebra giraffe, is an artiodactyl mammal that is endemic to the northeast Democratic Republic of the Congo in central Africa.

This skin sensation — often described as tingling, prickling, or numbness — is most familiar as the 'pins and needles' feeling after a limb falls asleep from staying still too long — name this sensation?
Paresthesia (or paraesthesia) is a sensation of the skin that may feel like numbness (hypoesthesia), tingling, pricking, chilling, or burning.
This herbaceous annual vine produces edible pods and comes in bush or climbing cultivars; global output hit 28 million tonnes in 2022, led by India. What legume species is it?
Phaseolus vulgaris is a herbaceous annual plant. Its botanical classification, along with other Phaseolus species, is as a member of the legume family, Fabaceae.

This medical condition occurs when air collects in the space between the lung and chest wall, typically causing sudden, sharp one-sided chest pain and shortness of breath — what's the condition called?
Pneumothorax is collection of air in the pleural space between the lung and the chest wall.
Originating in Central Asia despite widespread cultivation elsewhere, this is the most commonly grown species of a fuzzy-skinned stone fruit — what is its scientific name?
Prunus armeniaca is the most commonly cultivated apricot species.
Physicists denote this stretching of light's wavelength — caused by relative motion, gravity, or cosmic expansion — with the symbol z; its opposite is called blueshift. What is it?
Redshift is an increase in the wavelength, or equivalently, a decrease in the frequency, of electromagnetic radiation (such as light).
Sitting in group 4 just below hafnium, this synthetic element named for a famous physicist has a most-stable isotope that survives only about 48 minutes — which element is it?
Rutherfordium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Rf and atomic number 104.

Native only to groves on California's Sierra Nevada slopes, this conifer species includes the largest trees on Earth by volume, though fewer than 80,000 remain and it's now listed as endangered — what's the species?

Sequoiadendron giganteum (also known as the giant sequoia, giant redwood, Sierra redwood or Wellingtonia) is a species of coniferous tree, classified in the family Cupressaceae in the subfamily Sequoioideae.
Called sun spiders, camel spiders, and wind scorpions, these dry-climate arachnids are neither true spiders nor scorpions, and urban legends wildly exaggerate their danger — what order are they?
Solifugae is an order of arachnids known variously as solifuges, sun spiders, camel spiders, wind scorpions, and jerrymanders.

Tracing its lineage back to ancestral fish from the Early Jurassic period roughly 174 to 201 million years ago, this family of 27 fish species is one of only two living branches of an ancient order that also includes the paddlefish — name this fish family?
Sturgeon are the 27 species of fish belonging to the family Acipenseridae.

Equal to one weber per square metre, this SI unit of magnetic flux density was adopted in 1960 and named for a Serbian-American electrical engineer, on the proposal of a Slovenian engineer — name this unit?
Tesla (unit) (symbol: T) is the unit of magnetic flux density (B) (also called magnetic B-field) in the International System of Units (SI).

This parasite can infect nearly any warm-blooded animal, but can only sexually reproduce inside cats, and is famous for altering infected rodents' behavior to make them less afraid of feline predators — what parasite is it?
Toxoplasma gondii is a species of parasitic alveolate that causes toxoplasmosis.
This abnormal enlargement of the vein network draining the testicles is the most common correctable cause of male infertility, found in over a third of men with the condition. Name it?
Varicocele is an abnormal enlargement of the pampiniform venous plexus in the scrotum.
Neither an insect nor a parasite despite its common name, this terrestrial crustacean is one of the few of its kind to have colonized dry land, likely since the late Paleozoic — what is it?
Woodlouse are terrestrial isopods in the suborder Oniscidea.
Found naturally in coffee, bread and ripe fruit, this aldehyde is produced when your liver partly oxidizes ethanol — making it a chief culprit behind the hangover. What is it?

Born as a Spanish CASA design and now built by a major European aerospace conglomerate, this twin-engine turboprop transport plane first flew in November 1997 and entered Spanish Air Force service in 1999 — which aircraft?
Airbus C295: European tactical military transport aircraft.
A striking red-capped, white-warted mushroom of northern forests, this fungus may owe its name to an old use against flies — or to a medieval belief that flies caused madness. What is it?
Amanita muscaria: Species of mushroom. Amanita muscaria, commonly known as the fly agaric or fly amanita, is a basidiomycete fungus of the genus Amanita.
Consisting of a phenyl group attached to an amino group, this organic compound smells like rotten fish and serves as a key precursor to polyurethane and dyes — what is it called?
Aniline: Organic compound (C6H5NH2); simplest aromatic amine.
Its name comes from Greek roots meaning 'chief' and 'creator,' and historians often identify whole vanished civilizations by what survives of this visual art. What is it?
Architecture: Art and technique of designing buildings.

This rapid, irregular quivering of the heart's upper chambers can be entirely silent or bring palpitations and fainting — and it sharply raises the risk of stroke, dementia and heart failure. What is this arrhythmia?
Atrial fibrillation: Irregular beating of the atria of the heart.
Belonging to genus Fagus, this deciduous tree yields timber used for furniture, flooring, and plywood, and its wood also makes excellent firewood. What is this tree?
Beech: Genus of trees in the family Fagaceae.

After serving as creative director at Xanga in the early 2000s, this entrepreneur co-founded Twitter, then later launched a visual-search engine called Jelly that was acquired by Pinterest in 2017. Who is he?
Biz Stone: American blogger and co-founder of Twitter (born 1974)
Named in honor of physicist Satyendra Nath Bose and coined by Paul Dirac, this class of subatomic particle has integer spin and includes force carriers like gluons and the Higgs — what is it called?
Boson: Class of subatomic particle. In particle physics, a boson is a subatomic particle whose spin quantum number has an integer value (0, 1, 2,...).
Belonging to the superfamily Papilionoidea, these brightly winged insects pass through a chrysalis stage, and their oldest fossils date to about 56 million years ago — what are they?
Butterfly: Group of insects in the order Lepidoptera.
Also known as meridian fennel, this biennial plant in the Apiaceae family is native to western Asia, Europe, and North Africa — what is it?
Caraway: Species of plant in the carrot family.

Also known as gotu kola or Indian pennywort, this herbaceous perennial from the Apiaceae family is eaten as a vegetable and used in traditional medicine across Africa, Asia, and the Pacific — what is it?
Centella asiatica: Species of flowering plant in the celery family Apiaceae.
Packed with chlorophyll, this plant-cell organelle captures sunlight, splits water to release oxygen, and feeds sugar-making in the Calvin cycle — what is it called?
Chloroplast: Plant organelle that conducts photosynthesis.

Medieval German miners cursed an ore that looked metal-rich but smelted into nothing useful, naming it after a mischievous goblin — yet for centuries its blue pigment tinted glass and jewelry. Which element, symbol Co, atomic number 27, earned that goblin's name?
Cobalt: Chemical element with atomic number 27 (Co)
Considered the most renowned Greek mathematician since antiquity, he advanced measure theory and the calculus of variations and even gave thermodynamics an axiomatic formulation — who is it?
Native to the Andes and Mesoamerica, this plant genus includes five edible species known variously as squash, pumpkin or gourd — which genus?
Native to Madagascar and grown ornamentally throughout the tropics, this legume tree is known for its fern-like leaves and a flamboyant summer display of orange-red blossoms — what is it?
Delonix regia: Species of flowering plant in the bean family Fabaceae.
Also nicknamed the French Mastiff, this large, powerfully muscled brachycephalic breed ranks among France's heaviest dogs — which breed?
Dogue de Bordeaux: Dog breed originating in France.
One of the Hungarian émigré scientists nicknamed the "Martians," he extended Fermi's theory of beta decay and is colloquially called the father of the hydrogen bomb — who was he?

Dubbed a 'living fossil' and commonly known as horsetail, this spore-reproducing plant genus once included 30-meter-tall trees in Carboniferous forests, its node-spacing pattern said to have inspired the invention of logarithms — which genus?

With a rich chestnut crown and a bold black patch on each white cheek, this small Old World songbird nests in cavities, walls, or abandoned magpie nests, and lays five or six eggs that hatch in under two weeks — which bird?
Eurasian tree sparrow: Species of bird. The sexes have similar plumage, and young birds are duller versions of the adult.
Made by nearly every living organism, this protein locks iron away in a safe, soluble form inside cells, and its blood level is the standard test doctors use for anemia or iron overload — what is it?
Ferritin: Iron-carrying protein. Ferritin is a universal intracellular and extracellular protein that stores iron and releases it in a controlled fashion.
This Italian-American economist taught at MIT's Sloan School and Carnegie Mellon before collecting the 1985 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economics. Who was he?
Franco Modigliani: Italian-American economist and Nobel Laureate (1918–2003)

Sold under a non-proprietary name once the original patent expires, this type of medication shares the same active ingredient as its brand-name predecessor, though packaging and coloring may differ — what's it called?
Generic drug: Pharmaceutical equivalent to a brand-name product.
Bred at a Scottish estate by crossing a flat-coated gun dog with Tweed Water Spaniels, this gentle, honey-coated working dog was recognized by the Kennel Club in 1913 — which breed?
Golden Retriever: Scottish breed of dog. It is characterised by a gentle and affectionate nature and a striking golden coat.
Published in 1931 by an Austrian logician, these two results proved that any consistent axiom system for arithmetic will always contain true statements it cannot prove — what are they called?
Gödel's incompleteness theorems: Limitative results in mathematical logic.

This French mathematician reinvented what it means to find the area under a curve, publishing his sweeping new theory of integration in a 1902 dissertation titled "Integral, length, area." Who was he?
Strongly associated with human habitation and now the most widely distributed wild bird on Earth thanks to introductions across multiple continents, this small brown-and-black bird is which species?
House sparrow: Species of bird. The house sparrow (Passer domesticus) is a bird of the sparrow family Passeridae, found in most parts of the world.

Once diagnosed almost exclusively in women during the 19th century and studied intensely by Sigmund Freud and Jean-Martin Charcot, this term for 'ungovernable emotional excess' is no longer accepted as a medical diagnosis. What is it called?
Hysteria: Excess, ungovernable emotion. Hysteria is a term used to mean ungovernable emotional excess and can refer to a temporary state of mind or emotion.

He won the 1944 Nobel Prize for his resonance method of recording the magnetic properties of atomic nuclei, and was among the first Americans to work on the cavity magnetron behind radar and microwave ovens — which physicist?

A former Chicago options trader with finance degrees but no PhD, this entrepreneur co-founded a dot-com company whose peer-reviewed project evolved into the world's largest free encyclopedia — who is he?

Caused by a herpesvirus and linked to weakened immunity such as HIV/AIDS, this cancer produces purple skin lesions and disproportionately affects older Mediterranean men in its 'classic' form — which condition?
Kaposi's sarcoma: Cancer of the skin, integumentary lymph nodes, or other organs.
About 1.5 metres long and beginning at the cecum via the ileocecal valve, this final section of the human gut absorbs water and salt before waste reaches the rectum — what part of the body is it?
Large intestine: Last part of the digestive system in vertebrates.

Nicknamed the 'leopard slug' for its spotted grey-brown skin, this mollusc mates by dangling from a thread of mucus off a tree branch — which species, first spotted outside Europe in Philadelphia in 1867?
Limax maximus: Species of slug. It is among the largest keeled slugs, Limax cinereoniger being the largest.
As West Germany's economics minister, he engineered the postwar 'Wirtschaftswunder' before becoming the country's second chancellor in 1963 — who is he?
Ludwig Erhard: Chancellor of West Germany from 1963 to 1966.

Despite its fox-like markings, this leggy, reddish-coated canine of the South American savanna is neither a fox nor a close relative of more familiar canines, and it plays a key role dispersing fruit seeds — what is it?

This elephant-sized extinct genus of South American ground sloths, whose type species weighed up to four tonnes, was first identified from a fossil found on an Argentine riverbank in 1787 — which genus?
Megatherium: Genus of extinct ground sloth. The first (holotype) specimen of Megatherium americanum was discovered in 1787 on the bank of the Luján River in what is now northern Argentina.

This medical condition, usually diagnosed shortly after birth, is defined as a length at least 2.5 standard deviations below the average and affects about 1.5 in 10,000 male newborns in North America. What is this condition?
Known as simple sugars, these colorless, water-soluble crystalline compounds include glucose and fructose and serve as the building blocks of starch and cellulose — what are they called?
Monosaccharide: Simple sugars such as glucose and fructose.

This inner-ear condition brings on episodes of vertigo, ringing in the ears, and hearing loss lasting anywhere from 20 minutes to several hours — believed to stem from fluid buildup in the labyrinth. What is it?
Ménière's disease: Disorder of the inner ear. The hearing loss and ringing in the ears can become constant over time.
Its name literally means 'blue cow,' though only the males actually sport a bluish-grey coat — which is the largest antelope species in Asia?
Starting as a metals trader after the Soviet Union's collapse, which Russian billionaire built the Sayanogorsk smelter into the world's largest aluminium company, Rusal?
Created by Rasmus Lerdorf in 1993, this scripting language's name began as 'Personal Home Page' before becoming a recursive backronym meaning 'Hypertext Preprocessor' — what is it?
PHP: Scripting language created in 1994. PHP is a general-purpose scripting language geared towards web development.
Nicknamed "javelina" or "skunk pig," this social New World mammal travels in herds called squadrons and counts true pigs as its closest living relatives — what pig-like ungulate is it?
This anxiety disorder involves an irrational, excessive fear that persists more than six months and can trigger fainting in blood-or-injury cases — what is it?
Phobia: Anxiety disorder classified by a persistent and excessive fear of an object or situation.
Downgraded from planet to dwarf in 2006 when astronomers adopted a new definition, this Kuiper belt object orbits beyond Neptune—what celestial body is it?
Pluto: Largest dwarf planet. Pluto (minor-planet number 134340) is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt, a ring of bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
Sold under the brand name Phenergan, this first-generation antihistamine treats allergies and nausea but has also seen recreational misuse alongside codeine — which drug?
Promethazine: Sedating antihistamine. Promethazine is taken by mouth (oral), as a rectal suppository, or by injection into a muscle (IM).
Once one of America's leading rocket experts with an MIT aeronautics degree, he was deported to China in 1955 and went on to father that nation's space program — which aerospace engineer?

Nicknamed 'the Thud' by its crews, this Mach 2 jet flew most of the early Vietnam War's strike missions and became the only American aircraft ever pulled from combat over unsustainable losses — which plane?
Republic F-105 Thunderchief: US Air Force supersonic fighter-bomber.
Native to tropical Africa and the Indian subcontinent, this medium-sized parrot has established wild populations worldwide after pet-trade escapees adapted brilliantly to city life — which bird?

Rose-ringed parakeet: Species of bird. The rose-ringed parakeet (Psittacula krameri), also known as the ring-necked parakeet, is a medium-sized parrot in the genus Psittacula, of the family Psittaculidae.
This colorless, odorless nerve agent can kill within minutes of inhalation and was banned by the 1993 Chemical Weapons Convention — what is it?
Sarin: Chemical compound and chemical warfare nerve agent.
Domesticated more than 3,000 years ago and prized for having one of the highest oil contents of any seed, which crop is also known as benne?
Sesame: Plant cultivated for its edible seeds.
Known by the E number E211, this white crystalline salt of benzoic acid is a widely used food preservative and pickling agent — what is it?
Sodium benzoate: Common food preservative. It appears as a white crystalline chemical with the formula C6H5COONa.
A luminous ball of plasma held together by its own gravity, the closest example to Earth is the Sun — what celestial object is this?
Star: Large self-illuminated object in space.
